name: Battle of Sekigahara

phases.title: The Western Army stands on its ground
phases.text: Ukita's troops stood on the end of a mountain ridge with the Ishihara pass behind them, facing south-east. Konishi and Shimazu stood to their left, Toda and Hiratsuka to their right, and Otani and others at the foot of Mount Matsuo, with Kobayakawa on the mountain. Ishida had his headquarters on Kose-yama.

phases.title: Fukushima's vanguard goes for Ukita
phases.text: The Eastern vanguard under Fukushima moved against Ukita's troops. The fighting that began at about 8 am had not been decided by the middle of the morning.

phases.title: Ii and Matsudaira overtake Fukushima
phases.text: The troops of Ii and Matsudaira went ahead of Fukushima's men instead of following them, and engaged Shimazu's troops, who stood to the left of Ukita's on the Western side.

phases.title: The second wave rushes Ishida's troops
phases.text: The troops of Hosokawa, Kuroda, Kato, Tanaka, Ikoma and Takenaka rushed against Ishida's troops, the first of the Eastern contingents to come up against his position on Kose-yama.

phases.title: Oda and Todo move on Otani's troops
phases.text: Oda Urakusai and his son, with Tōdō's troops, went against Otani's troops at the foot of Mount Matsuo, to the right of Ukita and Toda on the Western line.

phases.title: Wakisaka, Ogawa, Kutsuki and Akaza attack Otani
phases.text: Wakisaka, who had been in touch with Tōdō, and the troops of Ogawa, Kutsuki and Akaza turned on Otani's troops beside them.

phases.title: Kobayakawa follows them
phases.text: Kobayakawa's troops, which had not moved, came down from Mount Matsuo after the others and joined the attack on Otani.

phases.title: Otani falls and Ukita's troops break
phases.text: Otani killed himself and Hiratsuka and Toda were killed. With Otani's troops gone from the foot of Mount Matsuo, Ukita's troops broke and fled from their ridge.

phases.title: Ishida's troops hold against Oda and Todo
phases.text: Oda's and Tōdō's troops broke through Otani's troops and turned on Ishida's. Ishida's troops held out against them for a time.

phases.title: Ishida's troops are beaten
phases.text: All of Ishida's men but those of Gamo were killed, and the rest fled towards Mount Ibuki, after they had held on against two Eastern attacks in turn.

phases.title: Shimazu's troops break through the enemy
phases.text: With the whole Western line in flight, Shimazu's troops had their retreat cut off. They tried to break through the enemy, lost Toyohisa, and left the field reduced to about fifty men.

note: Follows one account throughout, the Sekigahara gunki taisei of 1713, as summarised in the Japanese article; the Naifukō gunki and the Sekihara shimatsuki differ on the order of battle (for example Shimazu behind Ishida, the start at about 8 am against about 10 am in the Naifukō gunki) and on the course of the fighting. The account places the Western Army by named ground and by its neighbours, and says it faced south-east, so the Eastern Army is drawn on the opposite side. It gives the Eastern contingents only by the enemy each attacked, so their starting places are drawn opposite their targets, not stated. Where Kose-yama, the Ishihara pass and Mount Matsuo lay relative to each other is not given; they are placed beside their units. Not drawn: the Mori, Shishido, Chosokabe and Nabeshima troops at Kurihara-yama and the Kikkawa, Fukuhara, Natsuka and Ankokuji troops on Mount Nangu (the account does not say where they lay relative to the rest), Ishida's vanguard before Koike village, and the shot Ieyasu fired at Kobayakawa's troops, whose source of fire the account does not place. Konishi and Oda Nobutaka are drawn as one block as the account lists them together; the account does not tell what became of them.
